terms.gloss: what’s the use? what need is there?
terms.grammar: opus est, with the ablative of what is needed
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.127: quid opus est circumitiōne et ānfrāctū? (Lewis & Short s.v. ānfrāctus)
terms.comment: Literally “what need is there?”; what there is no need of goes into the ablative.

sources: Lewis & Short: opus
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 110.
